channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU moves to curb Airbnb‑style rentals in bid to ease housing stress
item.description: The EU's Affordable housing act lays out a comprehensive plan to curb tourist rentals, while giving power back to local regions. But is it doing enough?

item.title: [DW] German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

item.title: [DW] Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
item.description: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

item.title: [DW] Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
item.description: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic says it stopped scientists potentially developing bioweapons with AI
item.description: Start-up discloses five examples of when users ‘circumvented controls’ and made efforts to ‘obfuscate’ the purpose of their research

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘She killed me with her post’: Gaza students caught in Belgian minister’s immigration posturing
item.description: Belgium's immigration minister has gone on the warpath against evacuating 13 students from Gaza, but they might still be flying out despite her anti-Arab and pro-Israel dog-whistling.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine’s financial crisis resurrects Europe’s bitter dilemma on Russian frozen assets
item.description: The dire financial situation of Ukraine, ahead of what is expected to be a difficult winter with a possible further Russian mobilisation, has reopened the discussion on whether to use Russian frozen assets — raising difficult questions over legality, financial stability and Europe’s leverage in any future peace deal.

item.title: [DW] Germany’s Goethe-Institut is closing in Russia. Russians tell DW how canceled exams are upending their plans
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia affects their lives.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU asylum claims drop to lowest level in five years, but many still lost at sea
item.description: Despite increased calls to curb migration, asylum application numbers have been following a downward trend, due to geopolitical circumstances and EU cooperation with third countries. Migrants deaths on the journey, however, are far from dropping.

item.title: [EU Observer] Cleared in Greek border case, Austrian activist now sues EU data chief over Europol record
item.description: An Austrian national who helped document rights violations at the Greek Turkey border in 2020 is suing the EU's data protection watchdog over allegations it failed to protect her rights after Europol collected her personal information amid a Greek criminal case, for which she was later exonerated.

item.title: [EU Observer] ECB raises rates again as Strait of Hormuz disruption drives up gas prices
item.description: The conflict in the Middle East has pushed up energy-related inflation by 14.3 percent year-on-year

item.title: [EU Observer] EU moves to expand ‘outermost region’ privileges as Spain presses Ceuta and Melilla claim
item.description: The EU Commission says its 'omnibus' bill published on Thursday (10 September), will build on the special legal status that the so-called 'outermost regions' of the 27-member bloc have.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin spent over €110bn on Ukraine war so far in 2026, up one-third on last year (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,659)
item.description: New budget data and battlefield videos reveal a Russia quietly scrambling to finance soaring war costs, hide territorial setbacks and defend supposedly “safe” assets thousands of kilometres from the front.

item.title: [DW] Are electric vehicles really bad for the environment?
item.description: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s State of the Union AI data-centre dream will be a nightmare
item.description: As Ursula von der Leyen gears up to talk up her data centre plans in the State of the Union address next Wednesday (16 September), MEPs must question who will own and benefit from these data centres.

item.title: [EU Observer] Finland’s first licence to mine a Natura 2000 site would set a deadly precedent for EU nature protection
item.description: The Viiankiaapa peat bog in Finland faces permanent destruction for a short-term mining project. Even more worryingly, this could be a dangerous test case for the interests of mining for minerals overriding the public interest to preserve nature.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: why are European students falling behind?
item.description: The 2025 PISA results were published a few days ago. And they’re quite a bad surprise for most European countries. Educational performance is declining almost everywhere on the continent.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chinese Mission to the EU holds China-EU table tennis friendship tournament
item.description: Last weekend, the Mission of China to the EU and the Euroclub jointly hosted the China-EU Table Tennis Friendship Tournament in Brussels. More than 100 table tennis enthusiasts from China, the European institutions and the European Parliament participated in the event.

item.title: [DW] Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

item.title: [DW] US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

item.title: [DW] Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
item.description: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

item.title: [DW] Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
item.description: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

item.title: [DW] War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
item.description: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

item.title: [DW] Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
item.description: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
item.description: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Hamas planned Berlin-Vienna attacks for Oct. 7 anniversary, indictment shows
item.description: Prosecutors allege principal targets included Israeli diplomats, Jewish community centers and pro-Israel demonstrations.

item.title: [Financial Times] Bond markets stabilise after global sell-off
item.description: Decline in oil prices helps calm investor nerves ahead of crucial US inflation figures, but German borrowing costs edge above levels seen during Eurozone debt crisis

item.title: [Financial Times] Time to start taking AI risks seriously
item.description: Governments promise a light-touch regulatory agenda amid growing threats

item.title: [Politico Europe] Biotechnology at scale: Europe’s next competitiveness test
item.description: Biotechnology at scale: Europe’s next competitiveness Key findings Download the full report here:

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz’s ‘ethnic cleansing’ comments trigger defamation complaint from far-right AfD
item.description: The chancellor's remarks "crossed the line," according to a senior Alternative for Germany lawmaker.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU tech chief backs global AI rules in wake of extinction warning
item.description: "Global rules are really needed," European tech commissioner says after researchers sound alarm over AI risks.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany floats new Ukraine loan backed by frozen Russian assets
item.description: The idea would help to reduce the size of the EU's next long-term budget, per diplomats and officials.

item.title: [Politico Europe] 9/11 and the story America likes to tell about itself
item.description: Our history is filled with stories of enemies who underestimated us and good guys who ultimately prevailed. Twenty-five years after 9/11, that narrative looks different.

item.title: [Politico Europe] It’s been 25 years since 9/11. What has DHS become?
item.description: Even former secretaries now agree the department needs to be refocused or dismantled.

item.title: [DW] Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

item.title: [EU Observer] 25 years after 9/11, have the terrorists won?
item.description: As Donald Trump gambles on chaos at home and Vladimir Putin’s missiles pound Ukrainian cities, Timothy Snyder warns that Americans now face a new, self-inflicted 9/11-style test of whether they will - again - react exactly as the terrorists hope.

item.title: [Financial Times] IEA warns of ‘lost period’ in global oil demand
item.description: Strait of Hormuz will not reopen this year, agency says, warning of sharp drop in demand as refined product prices soar

item.title: [Financial Times] Scott Bessent fails to break ‘fever’ in US bond market
item.description: Treasury secretary’s $6bn bond operation is insufficient to stem the recent surge in borrowing costs, investors warn

item.title: [EU Observer] Magyar’s Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats and dismantles Fidesz’s county fiefdoms (Day 122 of the Tisza government)
item.description: By slashing the powers of Fidesz’s regional barons and kicking out a fifth of Russia’s embassy staff, Péter Magyar is trying to recast Hungary’s role in both its own hinterland and the wider European security game.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How Sweden’s tight election could normalise far-right power-sharing across Europe
item.description: With two blocs neck-and-neck, Sweden’s election could cement a new model in Europe where mainstream conservatives openly govern with the far right, reshaping EU debates on migration, energy and security.

item.title: [Financial Times] Houthis used Anthropic AI to try to build ballistic missiles
item.description: Missile test by group apparently failed, but exposes limits of AI safeguards

item.title: [DW] Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary's new tough stance toward Russia
item.description: Hungarian PM Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Budapest has expelled 10 Russian diplomats from the country. Moscow is considering halting gas supplies in response.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Emma Bonino, Italy’s activist commissioner, dies at 78
item.description: The lifetime public servant had a decades-long career straddling unpredictable national politics and the bloc’s evolving political system.

item.title: [Financial Times] US diesel hits record $6 a gallon on Iran supply shock
item.description: Surging cost for fuel critical to agriculture and industry stokes price pressures as Americans confront affordability crunch

item.title: [Financial Times] Bessent’s intervention risks damaging BoJ’s credibility, bankers warn
item.description: US Treasury secretary’s claims of insider knowledge could erode market perceptions of Japanese central bank’s independence

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump-Vance’s midterm pitch: vote Republican or live with the ‘lunatics’
item.description: Party far more comfortable raising fear of Democratic alternative than discussing own policies, including Iran war

item.title: [Financial Times] Iran and Gulf states to meet in push for Hormuz deal
item.description: Regional states hope temporary shipping agreement between Iran and Oman can offer a pathway to ease hostilities and reopen the strait

item.title: [Financial Times] Why Warsh is starting to bite back
item.description: The Fed chair has more political leverage — and skill — than many feared

item.title: [Financial Times] 9/11 and the America it left behind
item.description: The shock that briefly brought a shared sense of purpose has left a complicated legacy

item.title: [Financial Times] Europe’s difficult choices on AI
item.description: Data is the one area where it can still be sovereign and it has the greatest potential to generate growth

item.title: [Politico Europe] Drei Szenarien für einen Kanzlertausch
item.description: Neun Tage vor den Wahlen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Berlin schrillen im Konrad-Adenauer-Haus die Alarmglocken. Angesichts historisch schlechter Umfragewerte analysieren Rixa Fürsen und Hans von der Burchard die politische Zukunft von Friedrich Merz. Im Raum stehen drei konkrete Szenarien für eine mögliche Machtablösung. Vom freiwilligen Rücktritt bis zum konstruktiven Misstrauensvotum. Im 200-Sekunden-Interview stellt sich der CDU-Spitzenkandidat […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] California’s Newsom signs online kid safety laws, including rules backed by Sam Altman
item.description: The new state laws come amid rising concern that social media and AI pose health risks to children.
